acceptance: An ADR covering every semantic above is merged on joeharris76/todo-db main; for each it states the refusal code and the failure mode it prevents.
For each of the six 0.12.0 blockers the ADR names the new behaviour and the test that will prove it.
The ADR defines one store cutover from the current schema directly to the new schema behind the confirm flag, and states that older clients refuse with E_SCHEMA instead of reading the new state.
An independent reviewer that did not write the ADR reviewed it adversarially; the review record and dispositions are linked in this item's context and no Critical or High finding is open.

description:
todo-db 0.12.0 cannot run the integration-branch batch loop BenchBox adopted on 2026-11-01. Fixtures and code reads found six blockers: (1) any worker can take an unclaimed registered member, so the leader's later take fails (op_take, store.py:1596-1640); (2) a member without implementation dependencies must start exactly at the batch start head and a dependent one at the current integration head (store.py:1816-1819, service.py:1196-1199), so a member that merged in the current integration head cannot be prepared; (3) the integration head advances only inside prepare (store.py:1850), so no leader fix commit or develop merge can be recorded; (4) bind_batch_pr binds once and requires the head to equal the registered integration head (store.py:1528-1533), so the first review fix strands the final PR; (5) any update_item change, including context_append, deletes the member's receipt and its dependents' receipts (op_update, store.py ~1414-1425); (6) accepted files must stay byte-identical (service.py:1171-1182), which rejects legitimate same-file evolution, and a dead leader cannot be recovered without a live member claim.

Write a todo-db ADR defining the replacement semantics: owner-only take and takeover of active members; dispatch from the start head or any integration head this batch recorded; changed files measured from that base, with per-member frozen scope kept (service.py:1191-1193); recorded overlap instead of byte equality, with current-acceptance evidence required at final for every overlapped earlier member; receipts that keep the integration head they were integrated at; a leader-only advance of the integration head with a reason (fix or develop-merge), changed files and an expected previous head; a revisable final-PR binding (same repository, number and node id; head change guarded by the expected previous head; final evidence invalidated; exact retries idempotent); metadata-safe edits (context and context_append keep receipts; acceptance, needs, description and links edits still invalidate transitively, while scope has no edit path and registered batch metadata cannot be edited); guarded, audited owner recovery after a dead leader; a read path for the batch record; and a versioned capability with a new receipt schema, migrating the store once from its current schema directly to the new one.
